reps.brief:
YOUR ITEMS (account settings, taskId account-settings-delete-password, two bugs):
1) MAJOR: in local APKs Google sign-in is off (extra.googleSignIn.android=false). Cause: apps/mobile/scripts/build-apk.mjs builds and signs with this PC's own key (~/.sudoku-fight/apk-key) and sets SF_LOCAL_APK_SHA1 to its SHA-1, which Firebase doesn't list; app.config.ts then hides Google. But the QA phones run the app signed with the template debug keystore (apps/mobile/android/app/debug.keystore, SHA-1 5e8f16…f625, which IS listed in config/firebase/google-services.json): the main session re-signs each APK with apksigner using that keystore (it must, the installed app has that signature), so at runtime Google would work but the button/flows are hidden. Give build-apk a small, documented, tested way to say "this APK will be re-signed with key X" so app.config sees the right SHA-1 (e.g. an option like --resign-sha1 <sha1> or an env var read only by build-apk; or an option that signs with the debug keystore directly if the script already supports that); keep store/EAS builds untouched and keep assertStoreBuildWithoutDebugKey working. Update docs/BUILD-APK.md. Also: the app must never strand a Google-only user: with Google sign-in off, Settings → 'מחיקת חשבון' → 'המשך למחיקה' for a Google-only account (no password provider) opens a password dialog that can't work. Make it honest (e.g. explain that deleting needs Google sign-in, available in the store version, with t() in 19 locales) — check how the screen tells providers apart.
2) minor: in the password confirm dialog the red button 'מחק את החשבון לצמיתות' shrinks to about a third of the text size of 'ביטול' (adjustsFontSizeToFit / minimumFontScale in a half-width button). Moshe hates tiny text: the label must stay at the normal button size (wrap to two lines, or stack the buttons vertically when the label doesn't fit, per the app's existing dialog/button patterns). Check other ConfirmModal/dialog buttons with long labels in the 19 locales for the same shrink and fix them the same way.

items.id: account-settings-delete-password #1 (MAJOR): Google sign-in off in local APKs + Google-only user stranded at delete
items.rootCause: (a) scripts/build-apk.mjs always set SF_LOCAL_APK_SHA1 to this PC's own key (~/.sudoku-fight/apk-key). Firebase doesn't list that SHA-1, so app.config.ts resolveAppConfig set extra.googleSignIn.android=false. That happened even though the main session re-signs every APK with the template debug.keystore (SHA-1 5e8f16…f625, which google-services.json does list), so Google would have worked at runtime. (b) AccountSettings.tsx sent every non-Google-build deletion to the password step (`withGoogle ? 'google' : 'password'`, where withGoogle = googleBuild && methods.includes('google')). A Google-only account (methods=['google'], no password provider) in a build without Google got the 'אישור בסיסמה' dialog for a password it doesn't have.
items.fix: build-apk: new option `--resign-sha1 <sha1|debug>` ('debug' = TEMPLATE_DEBUG_KEY_SHA1; any SHA-1 with or without colons; a SHA-256 or garbage is refused). It means 'this APK will be re-signed with key X'. The new pure helper localApkEnv(keySha1, resignSha1) in lib/build-apk.mjs gives SF_LOCAL_APK=1 and SF_LOCAL_APK_SHA1 = resignSha1 ?? this PC's key, so app.config.ts checks the key the app is installed with. The build itself is still signed with the PC key, and checkApk/apksigner still verifies that. Combining it with --install or --install-only is an error, because the APK would be installed before it's re-signed. --dry-run prints a 're-sign' line, and the end of the build prints a reminder to re-sign. EAS/store builds are untouched: buildEnv deletes EAS_BUILD, isLocalApk is false on EAS, and assertStoreBuildWithoutDebugKey still throws. USAGE, d.mts, the app.config.ts comments and docs/BUILD-APK.md are updated (new section 'APK שייחתם מחדש במפתח אחר', an options-table row, the technical note). The main session should now build with `npm run apk -- --resign-sha1 debug`. Settings: when the build has no Google sign-in and the account has 'google' but no 'password' (`cannotConfirm`), 'מחיקת חשבון' opens a new notice dialog instead of the warning and password steps: 'צריך כניסה עם Google' / an explanation that deleting needs Google confirmation, that this version has no Google sign-in, and that it can be deleted in the store app (Google Play) / a single 'הבנתי' button. This uses a new ConfirmModal `notice` prop (one action, which takes the first focus). There are 3 new keys (settings.deleteGoogleOffTitle/Body/Ok) in all 19 account.json files, with Arabic LRI/PDI around Google and Google Play. i18n:check and --release both pass.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/__tests__/appConfig.test.ts adds 'an APK signed again afterwards (`npm run apk -- --resign-sha1 debug`, the QA phones) follows that key'. It checks parseApkArgs → localApkEnv → resolveAppConfig: Google is on with the debug key listed, off without the flag, off for an unlisted re-sign key, and a store build still throws. apps/mobile/src/__tests__/buildApk.test.ts adds a '--resign-sha1' parsing/errors test and updates the default options. apps/mobile/src/screens/account/__tests__/GoogleSignIn.test.tsx adds 'a Google-only account in a build without Google sign-in is told where to delete it, never asked for a password'. All of these fail on the old code: the helpers and option don't exist, and the old screen opens delete-confirm and then the password dialog.
items.deviceCheck: A) The APK needs a new build: `npm run apk -- --resign-sha1 debug`, then re-sign it with apps/mobile/android/app/debug.keystore as usual and install. 1. In the APK, assets/app.config should show "googleSignIn":{"android":true,...}. 2. On the phone signed in as 'אחוותא' (Google-only): הגדרות → 'מחיקת חשבון' → 'המשך למחיקה'. Expect the dialog 'אישור עם Google' with the button 'אשר עם Google ומחק', and NOT 'אישור בסיסמה'. Press 'ביטול'. Do NOT delete the account. 3. Sign out on one phone. The login screen should show 'המשך עם Google', and signing in with that account should work. B) On an APK built WITHOUT the flag (Google off), signed in with a Google-only account: הגדרות → 'מחיקת חשבון'. Expect one dialog, 'צריך כניסה עם Google', with the explanation text and a single button 'הבנתי'. There is no password field and no 'ביטול' button. 'הבנתי', Android back and a tap outside each close it, and the account stays signed in. Check it in English too ('Google sign-in needed' / 'Got it').

items.id: account-settings-delete-password #2 (minor): red 'מחק את החשבון לצמיתות' shrinks to ~1/3 size
items.rootCause: ConfirmModal puts the two actions side by side at flex 1.4 (gold 'ביטול') : 1 (red confirm). On a 360dp phone the centred dialog's row is 272dp, so the red button gets about 108dp, which leaves about 76dp for text after its 16dp padding on each side. The Hebrew label needs about 190dp. Button's outline label uses adjustsFontSizeToFit with minimumFontScale 0.7, but minimumFontScale is iOS-only. On Android the shrink has no floor, so the text was drawn at about 40% size. The same applied to any long ConfirmModal label in the 19 locales (de/fr/es/it/pt-BR/vi/nl/pl/ru/id deleteSubmit, en/id/ar deleteGoogleSubmit, and so on).
items.fix: ConfirmModal measures each label once, unseen: a hidden, accessibility-hidden, pointer-less Text layer inside the actions row, in the button's own label style (new exports from Button.tsx: buttonLabelStyle and buttonLabelInset). It also measures the row's width with onLayout. The new pure stacksActions(rowWidth, gap, actions) returns true when any label plus its padding is wider than its flex share. Then the actions stack: a column with gap 12 and the same order, each button full width with no flex share, upright (the pair-rule skew applies to a row only). Stacked buttons get wrapLabel='always', a new Button mode that also works for the danger and secondary variants. A label still too long for the full width takes a second line at its own size, and the button grows from its height (minHeight). No dialog label is ever drawn smaller than button text. Short pairs ('ביטול' | 'כן, להיכנע') stay side by side and skewed as before. This is generic, so every ConfirmModal in the app (surrender, level exit, sign-out, terms, invite, moderation, and so on) gets the same treatment in all locales. docs/design/components.md §14.2 documents it.
items.test: New file apps/mobile/src/components/ui/__tests__/confirmStack.test.tsx covers the following. The stacksActions unit cases, including the QA case (190dp label in a 108dp share stacks; a short pair doesn't; nothing is decided before measuring; a notice has the whole row). The measure layer uses the button styles, is hidden, and leaves no duplicate text or buttons for queries. A short pair stays a row with flex and skew. The long red label stacks into a column with no flex and no slant; the label has numberOfLines 2 and no adjustsFontSizeToFit; the button has minHeight buttonModal; this is checked at text scales 1, 1.15 and 2. A notice shows one action. In every layout language (19 plus en-XA), each account dialog label fits the stacked full width in at most two lines with no word cut. This file fails on the old code: no stacksActions or buttonLabelStyle, and no -actions or -measure testIDs. The existing ConfirmModal, Button and a11yAudit tests and the game, levels, moderation and home suites all pass (1554 tests run).
items.deviceCheck: Phone 3 (SM-A165F), Hebrew, font size 1.0, signed in with an email+password account: הגדרות → 'מחיקת חשבון' → 'המשך למחיקה'. reps.brief:
YOUR ITEMS (taskIds levels-new-game-small-phone, levels-lang-english, levels-xp-offline):
1) New Game screen (Home → 'שחק') at phone font scale 2.0 on a 360x780dp screen: row texts end with '…' ('Real opponents, in …', 'Practice vs b…', 'אימון לבד • לוח …'). items.fix: Added linesAt(fontScale, lines) to screens/home/parts.tsx. It returns the design's cap below LARGE_TEXT_SCALE (1.15, the same threshold the app's Button already uses) and no cap from 1.15 up. items.test: ModesAndGameType.test.tsx adds 'large text (en/he at 2, en at 1.3)'. items.rootCause: ChapterLine in LevelResultView built the accessibility label as t('result.chapterLine', { gate }). The gate argument was the visible line's lowercase fragment (result.chapterOpen / result.chapterNeed: 'the gate is open', meant to follow '· '). Checking all 19 locales, en, de, es, fr, it, nl, pl, pt-BR, ru, tr, id and vi all had this; he, ar, ja, ko, th, zh-Hans and zh-Hant have no case.
items.fix: New function chapterLineLabel(stars, max, gate, t) in screens/levels/levelWording.ts, used by ChapterLine for the label. It uses two new keys, result.chapterOpenSentence and result.chapterNeedSentence, added to all 19 locales: capitalized where the language has case ('The gate is open', 'Das Tor ist offen', 'Kapı açık', 'Проход открыт'...), and identical to the fragment in caseless languages. The visible text still uses the old lowercase fragments. The last chapter, which has no gate, gets a trimmed label. Added 'levels:result.chapterNeedSentence#need' to NUMBER_OK in scripts/lib/i18n-numbers.mjs, next to the existing chapterNeed entry. i18n:check and i18n:release both pass.
items.test: levelWording.test.ts adds 'the result's chapter line, spoken'. It checks the exact English and Hebrew labels ('This chapter: 0 stars of 30. The gate is open', '... The gate needs 20') and that the visible fragment stays '· the gate is open'. It also runs once per language for all 19 and checks that the first letter of the gate sentence equals its toLocaleUpperCase(lang). LevelResultView.test.tsx adds an English render test: the label is capitalized and the visible text still reads 'This chapter 0/30 · the gate is open'.
items.deviceCheck: Settings -> Language -> English. Play any stage to its end, or leave it, to reach the result screen. With TalkBack, or via the level-result-chapter content-desc in a uiautomator dump, the label must read 'This chapter: N stars of 30. The gate is open' (or '... The gate needs 20'), with a capital 'The'. The visible line must still show 'This chapter · N/30 · the gate is open' in lowercase. Optionally repeat in German, Spanish or Russian (capitalized there too), and in Hebrew, where nothing changes ('בפרק הזה: … . השער פתוח').

items.rootCause: Home's XP comes from the progress store (myProgress), not from 'me'. The stages' XP reaches it through the answer to the levels sync's PUT /v1/me/levels (onProgress). Each stage won in flight mode triggered a flush that failed, and LevelsSync backs off exponentially: 5s, 10s, 20s, ... up to 5 minutes. Nothing told it the connection was back: it only retried on its timer, on app start, sign-in or foreground, and while the timer runs a flush() returns 'waiting'. So after airplane mode was turned off, the PUT waited out the remaining backoff, which can be minutes. Meanwhile Home's focus read GET /v1/me/progress, which returned the server's XP without the stages, so 1,178 stayed. A restart flushes at once, which is why the XP then appeared. Also, an older progress read answering after the sync's answer could put the old XP back. The 'stages: 97 · ★ 121' line on the card updated because it comes from the local levels.db, not the server.
items.fix: Added retryNow() to LevelsSync and PracticeSync: it cancels the scheduled retry and flushes now, keeping the failure count so a phone that is still offline keeps backing off. appProgress.syncProgressNow() calls retryNow() on both syncs when someone is signed in and the app does not know it is offline. startProgress subscribes to useConnectivity: on the switch from offline to online it calls syncProgressNow() and refreshMyProgress(). HomeScreen's focus effect calls syncProgressNow() before refreshMyProgress(). The syncs' onProgress now goes through adoptSyncedProgress, which drops progress reads that were sent before the answer (forgetProgressReads), so an older GET can no longer overwrite the XP the sync just paid.
items.test: levelsSync.test.ts: 'QA levels-xp-offline: the connection back, retryNow sends at once'. It plays stages 48 and 84 offline, grows the backoff to 40s, then shows that flush() still returns 'waiting' while retryNow() sends both stages with xp 60 and clears the timer. A retryNow() while still offline backs off further. appProgress.test.ts adds 3 tests. (1) Connectivity going from offline to online sends the queued game past the backoff and reads progress again; syncProgressNow sends nothing while the app knows it is offline. (2) syncProgressNow, as called by Home's focus, sends at once. (3) A progress read sent before a sync's answer is dropped and the level stays 4. All 3 appProgress tests were checked to fail against the old behaviour; the levelsSync test cannot run on the old code because retryNow() did not exist.
items.deviceCheck: Phone 1, Hebrew, signed in (אורי). 1) On Home, note the XP. 2) adb shell cmd connectivity airplane-mode enable. 3) Home -> 'שחק' -> staged practice (the offline banner should appear on New game). Win 2 stages with new stars; each result shows '+N XP'. 4) Go back towards Home, then adb shell cmd connectivity airplane-mode disable. Wait about 15 seconds: the connection re-check runs every 10s while offline. 5) Stay on Home, or go to History and back to Home. Expected: within a few seconds, without restarting the app, Home's XP rises by 10 per new star (+50 per gate opened), and my player card shows the same XP. Also try turning airplane mode off while already on the stage map, then coming back to Home: Home's focus sends the pending stages and the XP updates.

rep.notes:
Checks run, all green: tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit (clean); eslint on all changed files (clean); npm run i18n:check and i18n:release (0 errors); prettier on changed files. Jest: progress, levels, screens/levels, screens/home, screens/player, screens/progress, screens/account, screens/legal, i18n, plus all of apps/mobile/src/__tests__ (e2e included), 162 suites and 2,883 tests in total. The server was not touched.

Points to be aware of:
(1) Jest's default window is at fontScale 2, so two existing tests that checked the caps were moved to PHONE (fontScale 1) with setWindow, and the large-text behaviour is now tested explicitly.
(2) linesAt also lifts the note cap of SectionLabel on other screens (Settings, PlayerCard, Progress, Interferences...) at large text. This is the intended direction; at 1.0 nothing changes.
(3) Not changed, out of scope: the Chip and offline-chip texts (numberOfLines=1, fixed height 22) and the friends buttons in 'list' mode (not the default since D100). If QA finds '…' there at font scale 2.0, it is the same pattern.
(4) The foreground trigger still uses flush() rather than retryNow(), so the existing behaviour is unchanged. The new triggers are the connection coming back (useConnectivity offline -> online, detected by the 10s recheck that runs only while a watcher is mounted: Home or New game) and Home's focus.
(5) prettier --write on parts.tsx reflowed one existing line ('const seams = ...' in ScreenHeader). Formatting only.
No adb, APK, deploy, npm install or git write operations were done.

issues.problem: ConfirmModal's new hidden measure layer duplicates every dialog label as real Text nodes. The layer is at opacity 0 and pointer-less, and sits at the top-start corner of the actions row, on top of whichever button is rendered first. TalkBack never sees these copies. The QA agent might: it finds controls by text through `uiautomator dump`, takes the first match in dump order, and the measure layer is the first child of the actions row. A non-compressed dump includes views that aren't important for accessibility, and opacity is not checked. If the copies show up there, tapping a label by its text lands on the wrong button. In a neutral dialog the first button is confirm, so tapping the hidden copy of 'ביטול' presses confirm. In a danger dialog the first button is cancel, so tapping the hidden copy of 'מחק את החשבון לצמיתות' presses cancel. This holds in the row layout and in the stacked one, in RTL and LTR alike.
issues.evidence: ConfirmModal.tsx: `<View style={styles.measure} pointerEvents="none" accessibilityElementsHidden importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants">{measure(cancelText…)}{measure(confirmLabel…)}</View>` is rendered before the buttons. `measure: { position:'absolute', top:0, left:0, right:0, alignItems:'flex-start', opacity:0 }`. apps/server/src/testing/qaAgent/index.ts findNode() returns `nodes.find(n => fields(n).some(f => f === q))`, the first exact text match. RNTL tests pass only because RNTL drops nodes hidden from accessibility, which says nothing about what uiautomator dumps.
issues.suggestion: On a phone, dump any ConfirmModal (for example Settings → התנתקות) and look for duplicate text nodes with the -measure-cancel or -measure-confirm resource-id. Either way, take the copies out of the dump: move the layer offscreen (for example top:-10000 or a transform), or unmount it once both widths are measured. Its bounds should then never overlap a button.

issues.problem: syncProgressNow() starts the practices' PUT and the stages' PUT at the same moment. adoptSyncedProgress takes whichever answer arrives last as 'my progress' and drops every progress GET sent before it (forgetProgressReads). Say a practice and some stages were both played offline, and the server stores the practice first but its answer arrives after the stages' answer. Home then shows XP without the stages. The GET that Home's focus or the connection-back handler sent alongside is dropped too, so the stale XP stays until the next refresh. The two syncs used to run on their own timers, so this race was rarer. The new tests cover only stages, not a mix of practices and stages.
issues.evidence: appProgress.ts: `syncProgressNow(){ void practiceSync().retryNow(); void levelsSync().retryNow(); }`. Both syncs use `onProgress: adoptSyncedProgress`, which calls `forgetProgressReads(); adoptProgress(...)` with no ordering between the two answers. HomeScreen calls syncProgressNow() and then refreshMyProgress(), so that GET is always older than the sync answers.
issues.suggestion: After the sync answers arrive, read progress again: for example, call refreshMyProgress() once both retryNow() promises settle, if either one sent something. Or keep the drop-older-reads rule but follow it with one GET. Add a test for offline practices and stages together.

issues.problem: Home's focus now calls retryNow() whenever the app doesn't know it is offline. If the server answers with errors (5xx, timeouts) while connectivity is 'online' or 'unknown', every visit to Home cancels the backoff timer and sends the PUTs again. The failure count still grows, but each focus skips the backoff.
issues.evidence: HomeScreen.tsx focus effect: `syncProgressNow();`. LevelsSync/PracticeSync.retryNow(): `this.cancelTimer(); return this.flush();`.
issues.suggestion: Let Home's focus use flush(), which respects the backoff, and keep retryNow() for the offline→online transition only. Or limit retryNow() to cases where the last failure was offline.

issues.problem: The ConfirmModal actions start as a row and can switch to a column one frame later, once onLayout has measured the labels. This happens on every opening of a dialog with a long label. With Reduced Motion the panel still shows through its opacity, so the jump could be visible, and the dialog's height changes after it appears. This is a layout jump, not an animation.
issues.evidence: stacksActions() returns false while rowWidth is 0 or labelWidth is undefined. Both come from onLayout in a later frame. The report itself says: 'The dialog may flip from a row to a column one frame after mount'.
issues.suggestion: Keep the actions hidden (opacity 0) until both labels are measured, or cache the measured widths per label string, then check on a phone with Reduced Motion on.

issues.problem: The new notice text for Google-only accounts in builds without Google sends users to 'the app from the store (Google Play)' in every locale. On iOS, googleSignIn.ios is always false, so the notice would appear there with a Google Play reference. Today a Google-only account can't sign in on iOS at all, so this is a theoretical edge.
issues.evidence: app.config.ts: `ios: false`. account.json, en: settings.deleteGoogleOffBody, '...You can delete it in the app from the store (Google Play).'
issues.suggestion: No change needed now. If iOS gets Google sign-in, or a Google-only session can reach iOS, make the store name depend on the platform.

items.rootCause: ConfirmModal puts the two actions side by side at flex 1.4 : 1. On a 360dp phone the red button's share is about 108dp, which leaves about 76dp for text, and the Hebrew label needs about 190dp. Button's adjustsFontSizeToFit has a minimumFontScale of 0.7, but that floor is iOS-only. On Android the label shrank to about 40%. The same applied to long ConfirmModal labels in many of the 19 locales.
items.fix:
ConfirmModal measures each label in its button's own style (buttonLabelStyle and buttonLabelInset from Button.tsx). The pure stacksActions(rowWidth, gap, actions) decides when a label doesn't fit its flex share. When one doesn't, the actions stack: a column with gap 12 in the same order, each button full width and upright, with wrapLabel='always' (a second line at full size, and the button grows from its minHeight). Short pairs stay side by side and skewed. This applies to every ConfirmModal in all locales.

The review's issues:
- MEDIUM (hidden duplicate labels in the uiautomator dump): fixed. The hidden copy of a label now exists only until that label is measured, usually one frame. It renders only when its width isn't already known. After that the measure layer is unmounted, so no copy of 'ביטול' or of the red label stays in the tree. During that frame the copy is transparent and drawn 10000dp above its place (transform translateY: −10000). The transform moves the drawing, not the layout the width comes from, so its bounds never overlap a button and Android doesn't treat it as visible to the user.
- LOW (row-to-column jump): mitigated. Measured widths are kept in a module-level cache keyed by variant, button size, font scale and label. Every later opening of a dialog with the same labels gets its final layout on the first frame, with no measure layer. Only the first opening of a given label in an app session can still flip, one frame after mount. On that frame the dialog is still at the very start of its fade-in from opacity 0, with Reduced Motion too.
- I chose not to hide the actions until they are measured. TalkBack's first focus (onShow → focus on 'ביטול') would land on an alpha-0 view. If onLayout ever failed to arrive, the buttons would stay invisible.
- LOW (Google Play named on iOS): not changed, as the reviewer suggested. googleSignIn.ios is always false, and a Google-only account can't sign in on iOS today.
